description: Ants rarely damage crops directly, but they protect sap-sucking insects such as aphids and mealybugs in exchange for honeydew.
damage: Help aphid, mealybug and scale populations grow
Some species carry away seeds or damage seedlings
control_measures: Control the aphids or mealybugs the ants are tending — the ants then leave.
Apply sticky bands on tree trunks to stop ants climbing.
prevention: Remove weeds and crop debris near the field
Check plants for aphids and mealybugs weekly
safety_warnings: Avoid broad-spectrum soil insecticides unless advised by an agriculture officer.

description: Bees are pollinators. They increase yield of fruits, vegetables, oilseeds and pulses. They are not pests.
control_measures: No control needed. Protect them.
prevention: Do not spray insecticides during flowering hours (spray late evening if a spray is essential)
Keep flowering border plants and a water source
safety_warnings: Many insecticides are highly toxic to bees — read the label before spraying near flowering crops.

description: Many beetles (flea beetles, leaf beetles, chafers) eat leaves, flowers or roots. Some, like ladybird beetles, are helpful predators — check before spraying.
damage: Holes or skeletonised leaves
Damaged flowers and fruit
Grubs feeding on roots cause wilting
control_measures: Hand-pick and destroy adults in small fields.
Spray neem oil (azadirachtin) or a registered insecticide at label dose if damage is heavy.
Light traps at night attract adult chafer beetles.
prevention: Deep summer ploughing exposes grubs to birds and sun
Crop rotation
Do not kill ladybird beetles (red/orange with black spots) — they eat aphids
safety_warnings: Use only insecticides registered for your crop, at label dose.

description: Caterpillars are the larval stage of moths and butterflies, e.g. fall armyworm, pod borer, fruit borer and bollworm. They are among the most damaging crop pests.
damage: Large holes in leaves
Bored fruit, pods or bolls
Damage to the central whorl of maize
control_measures: Hand-pick and destroy egg masses and caterpillars in small fields.
Use pheromone traps to monitor moths.
Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) or neem for young larvae; for heavy infestation, a registered insecticide (e.g. emamectin benzoate, chlorantraniliprole) at label dose.
prevention: Install pheromone traps and bird perches
Grow trap crops such as marigold around tomato
Deep ploughing destroys pupae in soil
safety_warnings: Use only insecticides registered for your crop, at label dose.
Respect the pre-harvest interval before picking vegetables.

description: Earthworms improve soil. They make tunnels for air and water and turn residue into rich manure. They are not pests.
control_measures: No control needed. Protect them.
prevention: Add organic matter and compost
Avoid unnecessary soil insecticides

description: Earwigs feed at night on soft leaves, flowers and ripe fruit, but also eat aphids and insect eggs. Usually a minor pest.
damage: Ragged holes in leaves and petals
Damage to soft fruit and seedlings
control_measures: Set traps of rolled wet newspaper or bamboo tubes overnight and destroy the earwigs in the morning.
prevention: Remove debris and hiding places near young plants
safety_warnings: Chemical sprays are rarely needed for earwigs.

description: Grasshoppers and locusts chew leaves and stems. Large swarms (locusts) can destroy crops quickly and must be reported.
damage: Chewed leaf edges
Defoliation of young plants
control_measures: Report locust swarms immediately to your agriculture department or Locust Warning Organisation.
For local grasshopper damage, spray neem or a registered insecticide at label dose.
prevention: Deep ploughing destroys eggs laid in soil
Keep field bunds free of weeds
safety_warnings: Use only insecticides registered for your crop, at label dose.

description: Adult moths do little direct damage, but they lay the eggs that become destructive caterpillars (borers, armyworms, bollworms).
damage: Their caterpillars bore into fruit, pods, stems and bolls
control_measures: Use pheromone or light traps to catch moths and to know when to act.
Watch for eggs and young caterpillars over the next 1-2 weeks; act early on caterpillars.
prevention: Install pheromone traps at the start of the season
Destroy crop residues after harvest
safety_warnings: Spraying adult moths is usually ineffective; target the caterpillar stage.

description: Slugs are soft-bodied molluscs that feed at night in damp conditions.
damage: Irregular holes in leaves
Slime trails
Seedlings eaten off at soil level
control_measures: Hand-pick at night or early morning.
Set traps (wet sacks, boards) and destroy slugs collected under them.
Scatter a band of ash or lime around beds.
prevention: Reduce dampness and debris around plants
Water in the morning, not the evening
safety_warnings: If using slug pellets, choose registered products and keep them away from children, pets and livestock.

description: Snails, including the invasive giant African snail, feed on leaves and young plants in moist conditions.
damage: Holes in leaves
Seedlings and young plants eaten
Damage to fruit near the ground
control_measures: Collect and destroy snails in the evening or early morning.
Use traps baited with wet leaves or fruit peels.
prevention: Remove weeds and moist hiding places
Keep field borders clean
safety_warnings: If using bait pellets, choose registered products and keep away from animals and children.

description: Most wasps are helpful: they hunt caterpillars or lay eggs inside pests (parasitoids like Trichogramma). A few can damage ripe fruit.
damage: Occasionally feed on very ripe fruit
control_measures: Usually no control needed.
Remove nests only if they are close to where people work, using protective clothing.
prevention: Harvest ripe fruit on time
safety_warnings: Wasps sting — do not disturb nests without protection.

description: Weevils are beetles with a long snout. Field weevils damage roots, stems and fruit (e.g. banana stem weevil, red palm weevil); others infest stored grain.
damage: Holes bored in stems, fruit or seeds
Wilting plants due to grubs in stems or roots
Damaged stored grain with holes and powder
control_measures: Remove and destroy infested plant parts.
Use pheromone traps for red palm weevil and banana weevil.
For stored grain, dry grain well and store in airtight bins; fumigation only by trained persons.
prevention: Use clean planting material
Keep the field free of crop residue
Dry grain to safe moisture before storage
safety_warnings: Never use storage fumigants yourself without training — they are deadly to people.
Use only registered insecticides at label dose.
